text:
maria: heads-up — running into a weird edge-only failure when swapping our auth fetch into middleware. Works locally with node but throws aborted errors on Vercel Edge.
kevin: can you paste the minimal repro? is it during startup or per-request?
maria: per-request. In middleware we do: fetch("https://auth.example/refresh", { method: 'POST', headers, body, signal: ctx.request.signal }) — sometimes it errors with `AbortError` immediately.
sam: hmm passing request.signal into downstream fetch in edge runtime is dodgy. Edge fetch implementations differ across runtimes (V8 vs Node). Are you using the Next Edge runtime (middleware.ts) or an Edge Function?
maria: middleware.ts on Next 14. Using Redwood JS SDK v0.9. Our SDK uses a helper that attaches an AbortSignal for retry/backoff. Might collide with Next's own signal.
alex: I saw a similar report — Next's middleware gives a ReadableStream request body and a signal that appears to be already aborted if the framework rewires the request for streaming. Could be timing: our retry wrapper creates a new AbortController then proxies signals incorrectly.
maria: repro gist: ```ts
// middleware.ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
export async function middleware(req) {
  // sdkAuthFetch wraps global fetch
  await sdkAuthFetch('/refresh', { method: 'POST', signal: req.signal })
  return NextResponse.next()
}
```
kevin: sdkAuthFetch internals?
maria: it does: ```js
async function sdkAuthFetch(url, opts) {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  const signal = opts.signal
  // forward outer signal to internal controller
  signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => controller.abort())
  // start with retry that may call controller.abort() on timeout
  return fetch(url, { ...opts, signal: controller.signal })
}
```
sam: that forwarding is fine in classic Node but on Edge you can get a pre-aborted signal (maybe from Next's own routing). Adding a listener to an already-aborted signal triggers the callback synchronously which aborts `controller` before fetch even starts.
kevin: aha — so controller.abort() gets called during setup — fetch sees aborted controller.signal and throws AbortError immediately.
maria: exact. Locally we don't see it because Node's DOM AbortSignal behaves differently. V8's polyfill for Edge fires immediate listeners.
alex: short-term fix: check `if (signal?.aborted) { /* fallback: don't attach, or recreate */ }` before adding listener. Also guard controller.abort calls with a microtask so fetch gets a chance to start.
kevin: another approach: avoid passing req.signal from middleware into internal retries. For middleware-level requests, prefer manual timeout logic instead of wiring signals.
maria: tried `if (!signal?.aborted) signal.addEventListener(...)` — reduced frequency but still saw rare races.
sam: you can also use `Promise.resolve().then(() => controller.abort())` in the listener to defer abort until next tick — that can avoid sync abort races in some engines.
alex: long-term: update SDK to detect Edge runtime (typeof globalThis.Deno !== 'undefined' || navigator?.userAgent includes 'V8')? Maybe too brittle. Better: normalize AbortSignal semantics in our helper and add explicit tests against Next's edge runtime in CI.
kevin: also typing/ESM issue: some customers import sdk as CJS in middleware and it pulls a polyfill that overwrites global fetch/signal behavior. We should ensure the Deno/V8 compat builds are exported as ESM-only with clear import guidance for Next/Edge.
maria: true — a dev hit us because they imported `require('redwood-inference-sdk')` inside middleware via a compiled CJS bundle — runtime shim conflicts.
alex: steps we need:
- patch sdkAuthFetch to guard against already-aborted signals and defer aborts (maria + sam)
- add a Next Edge middleware E2E test in CI using `@vercel/nft` or `vercel dev` container (kevin)
- update docs showing recommended import pattern for Next middleware (ESM default) and note CJS pitfalls (alex)
- add a small snippet for users: ```ts
// recommended
import sdk from 'redwood-inference/sdk' // ESM
export function middleware(req) { /*...*/ }
```
maria: will open a PR with the guard + test.
kevin: also add a one-liner in release notes: "Fix: avoid synchronous AbortSignal forwarding in Edge runtimes (Next middleware)" :tada:
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for canary tomorrow at 03:00 UTC — tag PRs with `canary` label to include.
sam: QA note: test both Vercel Edge and local `next dev` — different runtimes. Also try `wrangler dev` if we claim Cloudflare support.
maria: thanks — I'll include a small reproducible repo and add a note about ESM vs CJS imports and how that can affect global polyfills.
kevin: perfect. If anyone hits this before patch lands, temporary workaround: avoid passing `req.signal` to internal retry controllers or do `const safeSignal = req.signal?.aborted ? undefined : req.signal`.
alex: +1. Also add a TS typing note: our helper should accept `AbortSignal | undefined` and document semantics so TypeScript users don't assume forwarding always safe.
maria: ok PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 — includes tests and docs. ping me for review :)
kevin: reviewing now.
alex: thanks!
